title: Taxes, homes and a Las Vegas band
summary: Edison paid off $37,000 in income tax, bought houses, and led bands in Las Vegas at the Thunderbird, where he married.

story.theme_name: Meeting, marrying and raising a family
story.community_name: Meeting, courting and marrying: musicians' love lives

blocks.x: Did you save money during this time or were you living it up?
No, I was married and I bought a home, you know. I had a family, my daughter, so you can't -- if you have responsibilities, you know, that's not being alone, you know.
No, but you know, I just wondered whether you --
Well, I bought a nice home. In fact, I bought two houses. And -- but when I first started making money out here, I owed Uncle Sam about $37,000. So I had to pay him off first.
Uncle Sam, income tax. So then I had a band in Vegas. I went there for a year to work at Thunderbird and I had a band --
What sort of band was that?

Well, I had Jimmy Forrest. I had Ike Isaacs then. I had a band -- well, during the career of my band-leading days, you know, you get a chance to -- somebody will say, "Well, I've got Gloria Lynn going into Vegas at the Thunderbird for eight weeks. I want you to have the band."

And I'd get the band together, go there with Gloria Lynn. Then I had a band there for about six months with Georgie Auld. We had a band. I stayed around Vegas for about two, three years, you know, Las Vegas. In fact, I got married in Las Vegas, and my daughter was born in 1965 and naturally, if you're going to make a future for kids, you can't be as rambunctious as you were when you were single.
